newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: OPPOSITION KEEPS UP PRESSURE ON GUIDELINES
The Federal Opposition has vowed to keep up pressure on the Government to enforce the Coaltion-introduced ministerial guidelines.
Opposition Leader Kim Beazley says the level of integrity given to the guidelines needs to be established.
This follows the resignation of former Assistant Treasurer Jim Short over his ownership of ANZ bank shares, and questions over Peter Costello's wife's shareholdings.
Senator Short stood down after discovering he approved a new operating licence for the ANZ bank while holding shares in the orgnaisation.
Treasurer Peter Costello has been criticised over his wife's ownership of Commonwealth Bank shares, but Prime Minister John Howard says Mr Costello is not in breach of the guidelines.
INTEREST RATE CUT NEEDED TO SPEED UP ECONOMY
The Chief Economist of the National Australia Bank says the economy is slower than previously thought, and needs an interest rate cut to help move it along.
The latest business survey by the National Australia Bank has found business conditions remain subdued, with the September quarter's trading conditions contracted.
The NAB's Alan Oster, says given the weaker economic outlook, unemployment is likely to rise before coming back down to around 8.5 percent by mid next year.
Mr Oster says financial markets are expecting an interest rate cut in November, but that is dependent on further economic information due out in the next few weeks.
DRUG SEIZURE IN MELBOURNE
The seizure of 24 kilograms of heroin in Melbourne on the weekend has prompted fears young people will turn to amphetamines to feed their addiction.
It's expected the bust will cut off a main supply of heroin to the Streets of Victoria.
The high grade heroin was intercepted at Melbourne Airport and is estimated to have a street value of A$30 million.
Three men have been charged over the seizure, and will appear in court today.
SIEGE IN SYDNEY'S SOUTH
Negotiators are talking with a man who's been holding police at bay for more than 13 hours in a house in Sydney's south.
Police say the 43 year old man is heavily armed and holding his two young sons hostage.
It's believed the stand-off began following a domestic dispute.
More than 60 police are surrounding the Wonora Heights house.
PNG GOVERNMENT STUNNED OVER ASSASSINATION
In Papua New Guinea, the autopsy on the assassinated Premier of Bougainville, Theodore Miriung, has revealed he was shot four times in the front and back.
News of the assassination has stunned the PNG government which was about to reinforce the Premier's authority.
After being suspicious of Mr Miriung for months, Port Morseby was planning to increase his Transitional Government's power to restore services to the people of Bougainville.
Mr Miriung has no obvious successor and it's expected that few will now be willing to take the risks he did.
AUSSIE CRAWL BAND MEMBER DIES
Australian Crawl guitarist Brad Robinson has died in Melbourne, at the age of 38.
He was a co-founder of Aussie Crawl -- one of Australia's biggest rock bands of the 80's.
Robinson, who was diagnosed with cancer three years ago, was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame at this month's ARIA awards.
